rationale: Three concrete surfaces, all existing modules. (1) stryker.config.json mutate array (lines 8-29) gains an opencode-agent/src include with the !index.ts/!constants.ts exclusion pattern the existing entries use. (2) The staged-file dispatch is isGateableImplFile in .hooks/tdd/test-resolver.mjs:22-34 - it admits only src/, client/, plugins/, review-loop/src/, afk-runner/src/; it is consumed both by the write-hook checks (enforce-tdd, snapshot-surface, verify-no-new-surface, tdd-nudge, verify-tests-pass) and by the mutation gate's selectChangedMutationTargets (scripts/mutation/changed-files.ts:9,88,113), which is the single target selector behind plan/shard/gate (shard-plan.ts deps.selectTargets) and test:mutate:changed - so widening the gate to opencode-agent/src is a change in that one predicate (plus plausibly the sibling mappers suggestTestPath/findTestFile/resolveImplPath in the same file so tests/opencode-agent/x.test.ts resolution follows the review-loop/afk-runner pattern, and the 'must never narrow the mappers' pin at .hooks/tests/tdd/test-resolver.test.ts:320). (3) scripts/check.sh carries the workspace enumerations (is_license_header_file:55, is_oxlint_scoped_file:68 - both already list opencode-agent/src, so the change verifies/aligns rather than extends them). Baseline seeding writes scripts/mutation/baseline.json from the existing seed commands (test:mutate:changed --update-baseline / seed-from.ts; no new runner code needed). Tests that pin the touched behavior and will need the new root asserted: .hooks/tests/tdd/test-resolver.test.ts (roots + mapper pins), tests/scripts/mutation/stryker-config.test.ts (config pins), tests/scripts/mutation/changed-files.test.ts and all-files.test.ts (target selection from gateability + config globs). Docs that explicitly record the blind spot and must be updated: scripts/mutation/README.md:201, docs/architecture/commands.md:81, CLAUDE.md (mutation-testing paragraph naming opencode-agent/ as unmeasured). scripts/mutation/exclusions.ts is a plausible touch only if some opencode-agent file proves instrumentation-incompatible; shard-sizing.ts named numbers are design-record-only per the task, so no code change expected there. Not a new subsystem: every edit lands in an existing config/hook/script module; no DB, provider, or credential surface.
